newsitem.title: INDIA: Prudential to invest in Indian equities.
newsitem.headline: Prudential to invest in Indian equities.

text.p: Britain's Prudential Corp Plc will shortly begin to invest directly in Indian firms' equity as part of its $1.0 billion Prudential InvestDirect Asia Fund announced last November, its top officials said on Monday.
"We are looking at investments in the $10 million-$20 million band," Eric Sandlund, managing director of Prudential Portfolio Managers Asia told a news conference.
He said stock and bond markets in several emerging markets were too small for large investors to take an adequate exposure.
"This is clearly the case in India," Sandlund said.

"The $1.0 billion target for this fund will be financed from Prudential's own business with no reliance on external funding and the aim for 1997 will be to start the fund with $150 million," Prudential said in a statement.
The fund aimed to provide direct development capital for infrastructure projects and growing companies in emerging markets in Asia -- China, India and Vietnam in particular.
Prudential has appointed Credit Lyonnais Securities Asia as its fund manager.
"The quality of information from Indian companies and from the government is a plus point for India," said Josephine Price, managing director of Credit Lyonnais Asia Private Equity Fund.
Sandlund is a member of a Prudential delegation touring India visit to explore investment opportunities.
Prudential officials said they were looking at a time horizon of three to seven years for their equity investments.
Prudential's current investment in Indian equities, mostly through GDRs of Indian firms, is less than $100 million
Prudential preferred direct equity investments to the secondary market because of poor settlement procedures and sharp share price volatilities, its officials said.
"Establishment of a (share) depositary will be the most significant development in the Indian capital market in 1997," Sandlund said.
